what: A `cargo test --no-run` of another package, run while a 6-minute suite was queued behind cargo's lock, relinked `target/release/blaze` (a `#[cfg(test)]` edit in hir-ty-codegen changes the lib's source file). A client of the new binary then told the daemon of the old one `is another build of blaze ... stopping it and starting this one`.
cost: one suite run I had to reason about before trusting, and a rule for the rest of the session: no cargo while a real-driver suite runs
cause: the test target's `CARGO_BIN_EXE_blaze` is the one file every build rewrites; a daemon is tied to the exact binary
workaround: the suite now hard-links the engine and the thin `blaze` per test into CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/revisions-bin/<root> (real.rs `install`), so a relink that replaces the built file (a new inode) leaves each test on the binary it linked (not measured: a linker that writes in place would still reach it); `BLAZE_REVISIONS_BLAZE` names the engine and `BLAZE_REVISIONS_THIN` the thin (build it first: `cargo build -p blaze-thin`), each on that filesystem
state: workaround in place 2026-11-12 (real.rs `install`, edited by claude-opus-5-5); whether a relink during a run still reaches a test is not measured
